title: Use ESLint in Your Project

    title: Use ESLint in Your Project
    order: 1

This guide is intended for those who wish to use ESLint as an end-user. If you're looking for how to extend ESLint or work with the ESLint source code, please see the [Extend ESLint documentation](../extend/).

---
title: Extend ESLint
eleventyNavigation:
    key: extend eslint
    title: Extend ESLint
    order: 2
---

This guide is intended for those who wish to extend the functionality of ESLint.

In order to extend ESLint, it's recommended that:

- You know JavaScript, since ESLint is written in JavaScript.
- You have some familiarity with Node.js, since ESLint runs on it.
- You're comfortable with command-line programs.

If that sounds like you, then continue reading to get started.

request.instructions: The documents are sections of the documentation of ONE open-source project at one commit. Report a conflict only when two sections make incompatible statements about the SAME option, flag, default value, limit, version requirement, or behavior, for the same product version and scope. These are NOT conflicts: values of different options; example values in code samples that merely override a default; statements explicitly scoped to an older version or to migration history; one section giving more detail than the other; different defaults that the text ties to different contexts (per-route vs global, dev vs build, agent mode vs server mode).
